findings.highlight: the entrance exams for the new students will start next week
findings.evidenceJa: 再来週からは、とうとう新入生相手の商売が始まる
findings.explanation: The university finishes the academic year this weekend, and the business or activity aimed at incoming freshmen begins the week after next. The English turns that into entrance exams beginning next week, changing both the event and its timing.
findings.japanese:
峰城大は、今週末をもって本年度の課程を修了し、
再来週からは、とうとう新入生相手の商売が始まる。
findings.todokanai: All of Houjou University's courses for this year will be finished by the end of the week. And the entrance exams for the new students will start next week.

findings.highlight: Whenever I lectured him about women before, he never paid attention to me
findings.evidenceJa: 俺が女のことで説教するたびに、目の前の友がいつも呟いてたっけ
findings.explanation: Haruki recalls that Takeya used to mutter this same 'haven't you learned?' reproach whenever Haruki lectured him about women. The English instead says Takeya ignored Haruki's lectures, erasing the comic callback in which their moral roles have now completely reversed.
findings.japanese:
…って、俺が女のことで説教するたびに、
目の前の友がいつも呟いてたっけ。
findings.todokanai: …Whenever I lectured him about women before, he never paid attention to me.

findings.explanation: Haruki says Takeya's failed week in the theatre club makes complete sense; the English says he is glad Takeya failed miserably.

findings.highlight: she never cared about it one bit
findings.evidenceJa: あの女はそんなことカケラも覚えてなかった
findings.explanation: Chiaki did not remember Takeya's humiliating rejection at all, exemplifying how she forgets people and events once the performance ends. The English says she never cared, replacing her defining discontinuity of memory with ordinary cruelty.
findings.japanese:
「ところがあの女はそんなことカケラも覚えてなかった。
…そういう奴だよ」
findings.todokanai: "But she never cared about it one bit. …That's the type of person she is."

findings.highlight: "That's why Haruki… I won't speak ill of you. But that woman is just…"
findings.evidenceJa:
「だから春希…
悪いこと言わない。あの女だけは…」
findings.explanation: 悪いこと言わない is an idiom meaning 'take my advice' or 'I say this for your own good'; the English says Takeya will not speak ill of Haruki.
findings.japanese:
「だから春希…
悪いこと言わない。あの女だけは…」
findings.todokanai: "That's why Haruki… I won't speak ill of you. But that woman is just…"

findings.highlight: "That's exactly what I had in mind…"
findings.evidenceJa: 「頭ではわかってるつもりですよ…」
findings.explanation: Yoshida says he understands the danger intellectually; the English says it was exactly what he had in mind.
findings.japanese: 「頭ではわかってるつもりですよ…」
findings.todokanai: "That's exactly what I had in mind…"

findings.explanation: After explicitly saying carnal desire is rising in her, Chiaki says she wants Haruki to take or sleep with her. 'I want to be held' permits an innocent embrace and blunts the deliberately sexual third item in her list of physical appetites.
findings.japanese: 「あぁ、おなかすいた、眠い…抱かれたい～」
findings.todokanai: "Ahh, I'm hungry, I'm sleepy… I want to be held～"

findings.highlight: I haven't done that with you for three days now
findings.evidenceJa: どれも三日くらい前からしてないんだもん
findings.explanation: Chiaki says she has had none of the three things she just named—food, sleep, and sex—for about three days. The English collapses them into an unspecified act she has not done 'with you,' making the claim nonsensical after Haruki's absence and obscuring her dangerous total exhaustion.
findings.japanese:
「だってさ～。
どれも三日くらい前からしてないんだもん」
findings.todokanai: "I mean, come on～ I haven't done that with you for three days now."

findings.highlight: a sense of pity I'm feeling willingly
findings.evidenceJa: そして自分勝手な憐憫を
findings.explanation: Haruki identifies the last of his unprecedented feelings toward Chiaki as selfish pity, condemning his own compulsion to rescue her. The English calls it pity he feels 'willingly,' which does not convey the moral self-indictment and is barely intelligible.
findings.japanese:
恐怖と、怒りと、焦燥と…
そして自分勝手な憐憫を。
findings.todokanai: There's fear, anger, unease… and a sense of pity I'm feeling willingly.

findings.highlight: Are you trying to predict my future many years from now
findings.evidenceJa: あたしの数年先にいるつもりなの？　春希
findings.explanation: Chiaki asks why Haruki assumes he will witness her ruin—whether he intends to still be there, in her life, several years from now. The English makes this a question about predicting her future, removing the startled romantic implication of his long-term presence.
findings.japanese:
「…どうして、あたしが破滅するところを見るの？
あたしの数年先にいるつもりなの？　春希」
findings.todokanai: "…How do you know you'll see me fail? Are you trying to predict my future many years from now, Haruki?"

findings.highlight: "My appetite has been replaced by an immense lust recently. I get so engrossed in writing the script that I find myself doing it before I know it. …Furiously masturbating, that is…"
findings.evidenceJa:
「あたし最近さぁ、食欲がない代わりに性欲が凄くてさ、
ホン書きに詰まると、ついついしちゃうんだよね。
…激しいオナニー」
findings.explanation: Chiaki masturbates when she gets stuck writing; the English says it happens because she gets engrossed in writing.
findings.japanese:
「あたし最近さぁ、食欲がない代わりに性欲が凄くてさ、
ホン書きに詰まると、ついついしちゃうんだよね。
…激しいオナニー」
findings.todokanai: "My appetite has been replaced by an immense lust recently. I get so engrossed in writing the script that I find myself doing it before I know it. …Furiously masturbating, that is…"

findings.highlight: Well, I'm now stuck in a situation where I can't escape from her little cat charade…
findings.evidenceJa: で、そんな投げっぱなしの猫芝居で逃げられた俺は…
findings.explanation: Chiaki escapes the serious exchange by abandoning it inside an unresolved cat performance; the English says Haruki cannot escape her cat charade.
findings.japanese: で、そんな投げっぱなしの猫芝居で逃げられた俺は…
findings.todokanai: Well, I'm now stuck in a situation where I can't escape from her little cat charade…
